fixes.explanation: Oh, I wish it worked that way, friend, but it doesn't. God says, "Will not your creditors suddenly arise and those who disturb you awaken? Then you will become their prey." (Habakkuk 2:7). The verse has them waking up and rising, not forgetting a thing. I bet they brought their receipts.

Right, baker. The verse asks, "Will not your creditors suddenly arise and those who disturb you awaken? Then you will become their prey." (Habakkuk 2:7). Those who are owed wake up and rise suddenly. He becomes their prey, and the verse says nothing about them forgetting.

True, baker. "Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed and establishes a town by iniquity!" (Habakkuk 2:12). That's woe number three. The woe before it was about a house in verse 9, and this one is about a city built with bloodshed.

Moab is a fair guess, baker, but it's not the name in this verse. God says, "For your violence against Lebanon will overwhelm you…" (Habakkuk 2:17). Lebanon is the place named, and the same verse says the destruction of animals will terrify him. Keep your eyes on the name the verse gives.

Right, baker. "For its maker trusts in his own creation; he makes idols that cannot speak." (Habakkuk 2:18). He's counting on something that can't say a single word back. The verse even calls the idol a teacher of lies.

Yes, baker. "But the LORD is in His holy temple…" (Habakkuk 2:20). After all that talk of silent idols, this is the one who is there. The idols have gold on them, and there's no breath in them. Then comes the call: "let all the earth be silent before Him."

Not quite, friend. The verse says, "But the LORD is in His holy temple…" (Habakkuk 2:20). A high mountain sounds grand, but that's not what the verse says. It puts Him in His holy temple, and then comes the call, "let all the earth be silent before Him."
